<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par87" />Undoubted instances of masculines with (masculine) plural in {{GHGheb|text=־וֹת}} are: {{GHGheb|text=אָב|translate=father}}, {{GHGheb|text=אוֹצָר|translate=treasure}}, {{GHGheb|text=בֹּאר}} and {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹר|translate=cistern}}, {{GHGheb|text=זָנָב|translate=tail}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֲלוֹם|translate=dream}}, {{GHGheb|text=כִּסֵּא|translate=throne}}, {{GHGheb|text=לֵב}} and {{GHGheb|text=לֵבָב|translate=heart}}, {{GHGheb|text=לוּחַ|translate=tablet}}, {{GHGheb|text=לַ֫יִל}} and {{GHGheb|text=לַ֫יְלָה|translate=night}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִזְבֵּחַ|translate=altar}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָקוֹם|translate=place}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֹאד|translate=skin-bottle}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֵר|translate=lamp}}, {{GHGheb|text=עוֹר|translate=skin}}, {{GHGheb|text=קוֹל|translate=voice}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֻׁלְחָן|translate=table}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁם|translate=name}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹפָר|translate=trumpet}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|q}}
Feminines ending in {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} which take in the plural the termination {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}} are {{GHGheb|text=אֵלָה|translate=terebinth}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֵימָה|translate=terror}} (but also {{GHGheb|text=אֵימוֹת}}), {{GHGheb|text=דְּבֵלָה|translate=a cake}} of figs, {{GHGheb|text=חִטָּה|translate=wheat}}, {{GHGheb|text=לְבֵנָה|translate=a brick}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִלָּה}} (only in poetry) ''a word'', {{GHGheb|text=סְאָה|translate=seā}}, ''a dry measure'', {{GHGheb|text=שְׂעוֹרָה|translate=barley}}, and the following names of animals {{GHGheb|text=דְּבוֹרָה|translate=a bee}} and {{GHGheb|text=יוֹנָה|translate=a dove}}; also, for {{GHGheb|text=בֵּיצִים}} fem. ''eggs'', a singular {{GHGheb|text=בֵּיצָה}} is to be assumed. {{GHGheb|text=אֲלֻמָּה|translate=sheaf}} and {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנָה|translate=year}} (see above, n) take both {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}}; cf. finally {{GHGheb|text=שִׁבֹּ֫לֶת|translate=an ear of corn}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=שִׁבֳּלִים}}, and without the fem. termination in the singular {{GHGheb|text=פִּילֶ֫גֶשׁ|translate=concubine}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=פִּֽילַגְשִׁים}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|r}}
'''5.''' A strict distinction in gender between the two plural endings is found, in fact, only in adjectives and participles, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=טוֹבִים|translate=boni}}, {{GHGheb|text=טוֹבוֹת|translate=bonae}}, {{GHGheb|text=קֹֽטְלִים}} masc., {{GHGheb|text=קֹֽטְלוֹת}} fem. So also in substantives of the same stem, where there is an express distinction of sex, as {{GHGheb|text=בָּנִים|translate=filii}}, {{GHGheb|text=בָּנוֹת|translate=filiae}}; {{GHGheb|text=מְלָכִים|translate=reges}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְלָכוֹת|translate=reginae}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|s}}
Rem. 1. In some few words there is added to the plural ending {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} a second (masculine) plural termination (in the form of the ''constr. st''. {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}}, cf. {{GHGpar|89|c}}), or a dual ending {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ יִם}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בָּמָה|translate=a high place}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=בָּמוֹת}}, ''constr. st''. {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽמוֹתֵי}} (also {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽמֳתֵי}} ''bām<sup>o</sup>thê'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=8}}, &c., sometimes as ''Q<sup>e</sup>rē'' to the K<sup>e</sup>thîbh {{GHGheb|text=במותי}}; see {{GHGpar|95|o}}); {{GHGheb|text=מֵרַאֲשֹׁתֵי שָׁאוּל}} ''from Saul’s head'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=26|verse=12}}; {{GHGheb|text=חוֹמָה|translate=wall}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=חוֹמוֹת|translate=moenia}}, whence dual {{GHGheb|text=חוֹמֹתַ֫יִם|translate=double walls}}. This double indication of the plural appears also in the connexion of suffixes with the plural ending {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} ({{GHGpar|91|m}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|t}}
2. Some nouns are only used in the singular (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אָדָם|translate=man}}, and collectively ''men''); a number of other nouns only in the plural, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מְתִים|translate=men}} (the old ''sing''. {{GHGheb|text=מְתוּ}} is only preserved in proper names, see {{GHGpar|90|o}}; in Eth. the ''sing.'' is ''mĕt'', man); some of these have, moreover, a singular meaning ({{GHGpar|124|a}}), as {{GHGheb|text=פָּנִים|translate=face}}. In such cases, however, the same form can also express plurality, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=פָּנִים}} means also ''faces'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=1|verse=6}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים|translate=God}}, and also ''gods'' (the ''sing.'' {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהַּ}}, a later formation from it, occurs only ten times, except in Job forty-one and in Daniel four times).
<section end="par87" />
<section begin="par88" />{{GHGpar-heading|88|Of the Dual}}

<div style="font-size: small; text-align: center;">Cf. the literature on the Semitic dual in Grünert, ''Die Begriffs-Präponderanz und die Duale a potiori im Altarab''. (Wien, 1886), p. 21; Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, p. 455 ff.</div>

{{GHGmargin-letter|88|a}}
'''1.''' The ''dual'' is a further indication of number, which originated in early times. In Hebrew, however, it is almost exclusively used to denote those objects which naturally occur in pairs (see e). The dual termination is never found in adjectives, verbs, or pronouns. In the noun it is indicated in both genders by the termination {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ יִם}}<section end="par88" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
